verdicts.why: This is the Spider-Man (1994) Lizard. The Marvel Database files Curt Connors as Earth-92131, the same as his twin, so a null Earth wrongly puts him on Earth-199999.
This is The Spectacular Spider-Man's Lizard. The Marvel Database gives Curtis Connors Reality = Earth-26496, the same as his twin.
This is the 1994 series' Venom. The Marvel Database gives Edward Brock Reality = Earth-92131, the same as his twin.

Confirmed in season 2 episode 13: Warren blackmails Connors, and he leaves ESU with Martha and Billy for the Florida Everglades. That is a real departure. The value is amended to match how the data records a departure elsewhere: an Independent stage plus left, with a title on the first stage now that there are two.

B. Reilly Investigations and Reilly & Ruiz Private Investigators are the same firm. In episode 8 it is only renamed when Janet becomes a partner, so this is no move. Under the rules a different but correct name for the same group passes, and all of it happens in the one title.

Eddie is a Bugle reporter on screen from episode 1. Jameson fires him in episode 2 and again in episode 9, before he bonds with the symbiote in episode 10, so the firing is a real departure in Spider-Man (1994). Keep the Bugle stage and add the departure rather than putting him outside the Bugle from the start. Also, the Marvel Database lists the Bugle as a current group, because of X-Men '97, not as a former one.

Same as his twin: he works at the Bugle on screen from episode 1 and is fired in episodes 2 and 9, before Venom in episode 10. The firing is a departure in Spider-Man (1994), so it is recorded as Bugle, then Independent, plus left.

In Spider-Man (1994) episode 43, his first step in story order, Steve volunteers for the Allies' super-soldier experiment and becomes Captain America. So the soldier stage starts in that title, not in X-Men: TAS episode 73. As the proposal says, both stages now share the same title, so check how the app resolves that before applying.
In Into the Spider-Verse, Spider-Woman saves George from being shot while he is on duty as a police officer, so the NYPD stage starts there. He quits the force in Across the Spider-Verse.

The Marvel Database says that after Miles escapes, Hobie goes home 'stating that he was quitting the Spider Society' and later joins Gwen's band. That is a real departure in Across the Spider-Verse, and the value matches Gwen's record.

Confirmed: in episode 3, Big Donovan forces Lonnie to join the 110th in place of his brother Andre. In episode 1 he is only Peter's friend. But the app has no title called 'Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man (episode 3)'. The show has a single title, so both stages use that title.
The Marvel Database files him as Alonzo Lincoln, Reality = Earth-86445, the same as his twin. A null Earth wrongly puts him on Earth-199999.
Same as his twin: he joins the gang in episode 3 (Wikipedia, episode 3 summary). The invented episode title is replaced with the show's single title, which the app uses.

Rejected. The Marvel Database's own reality page gives the EarthNumber as Earth-688. The 'B' in the page name only tells the film version apart from the comics reality of the same number, and the film shows Earth-688 on screen. The app's Earth rule (EARTH.md) uses the number shown on screen, so changing it would be a rename for style.

This is the 1994 series' Morbius. The Marvel Database files Michael Morbius as Earth-92131, the same as his twin A:sv-michael-morbius-1994.
This is Raimi's Doctor Octopus. The Marvel Database gives Otto Octavius Reality = Earth-96283, the same as his twin.

The Marvel Database says Pavitr 'also became a member of the Spider Society', and Jessica Drew calls him in to help Gwen against the Spot. Joining Gwen's band at the end is not treated as leaving the Society for Peni or Peter B. Parker either.

The Marvel Database, citing X-Men: TAS season 5 episode 11, says that in World War II he 'fought ... as a member of the Howling Commandos' as a sergeant. He is S.H.I.E.L.D. Director in Spider-Man (1994) from episode 13. Its affiliations list both groups.

Confirmed: he 'decided to join Jameson and the Resistance' and only later 'found work as a photographer at the Daily Byte', so the order is right. The app already names this group 'The Rebellion' (X-51, John Jameson, Karen O'Malley and others), so use that name, not 'Human Rebels'.

The Spider-Men team ends when Spider-Carnage is defeated in episode 65, and the Marvel Database marks it Defunct. Peter's page lists the Daily Bugle as current and the Spider-Men as former, and X-Men '97 episode 1 has him covering the Gala for the Bugle.

Confirmed: the team ends in the Spider Wars two-parter (episodes 64 and 65), the Marvel Database marks it Defunct, and Octo-Spidey's page lists the Spider-Men as a former group. The value is written out in the data's departure form: an Independent stage plus left, with a title on the first stage.
Kraven the Hunter (2024) is an SSU film. The Marvel Database's Earth-688B page gives EarthNumber = Earth-688, which matches his twin A:sv-sergei-kravinoff and the other SSU records. Null is wrong.

Confirmed: the Marvel Database lists 'Human Rebels; Formerly: Machine Men'. In episode 5 he breaks his programming and is brought into the Freedom Fighters. But '(from the start)' is only used for a single group, so both stages take his one title.
